html:
The siege of Uthman's house was the revolt of discontented troops and settlers against the caliph Uthman in Medina, which ended with his killing in June 656.

Uthman, the third caliph, was from the Umayyad family of the quraysh. His critics said he favoured his relatives with governorships and wealth. Groups from Egypt, Kufa and Basra came to Medina with demands, and when they were not met they surrounded his house for weeks. A group of the rebels broke in and killed the aged caliph, who was reading the Quran.

It was the first time Muslims had killed their own caliph. The community split over whether the murderers should be punished at once, and Ali, chosen as the next caliph, was blamed by some for not acting. This led to the Battle of the Camel and the First Fitna.
sum: The siege of Uthman's house was the revolt of discontented troops and settlers against the caliph Uthman in Medina, which ended with his killing in June 656.
